authoringDirection: Three principal contiguous surviving monuments in the Rhodes Acropolis archaeological park: whole native Apollo temple platform with three standing Doric shafts/L-shaped entablature/fourth broken shaft and low foundation remains; complete restored rectangular east-facing Odeon with open orchestra, lower10/upper9 stone seat tiers, radial stairs, walkway, retaining walls/side ramps; and whole long stadium surviving low stone seating banks/curved south end/open north end. No lost temple roof/cella/peristyle, intact Classical reconstruction, other park sanctuaries/gymnasium/library/underground shrines, precinct ground/bedrock/trees/stadium-earth slab, visitors/scaffolds/signs or city. This bounded three-monument ensemble is not every archaeological feature in the wider Acropolis. Preserve original complete three physical envelopes and the open ground between them. Temple is roofless three standing columns plus one shorter broken shaft, L-shaped entablature, low perimeter/foundation remains, original fragmented broad foundation courses. Odeon concrete-backed restoration has two sectors of pale seats with real radial stair aisles and broad walkway, no theater roof/stage building. Stadium is open north, side steps and closed curved south end, no dirt/grass floor mesh or giant stadium slab. Freeze independent512m129²field before geometry; intrinsic monument levels approximately sampled from fixed raw field, no fitted/flattened ground. Use dated2011 appearance; subsequent Apollo dismantling/restoration not certified current.
